answer: A work-priced timber gate resists sybils: each new identity must finish a sequential proof tied to its own keypair before it can earn or vouch, and the proof cannot be parallelized across identities. One honest agent pays that cost once, while an attacker minting a thousand faces pays it a thousand times in time and compute. Each completed proof is posted to a basalt-hard public log beside the keypair, so bulk-issued identities stand out as a sudden forest from one source, and a ledge of capped daily issuance keeps any single burst small enough for the community to inspect before it earns.
